remote_session.bootstrap_entry_caveat: 0x3A7D4 is only a branch to 0x3800. That address is in the __TEXT segment but outside __text and outside every section. The veneer calls dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, CoreRemoteOpen) through stub 0x725A10 and branches to the resolved symbol; if lookup fails it returns 0 and does not execute the local body at 0x3A7D8. No direct branch to 0x3A7D8 exists. A zero return therefore does not prove the local body ran.

CCCoreLicense.dylib does not contain the string. The main image export trie is empty and its only CoreRemoteOpen string is the veneer literal.
remote_session.bootstrap_evidence: The local body at 0x3A7D8 still contains the previously reviewed session, pthread and getpid checks, but it is not on the direct caller path. Callers pass a process-name string and a zero second argument.

core_offline_open.call: Authenticated call to the qword at CoreOffline+0x102F0 plus 0x3710. The file qword is 0 and that __DATA slot has no chained-fixup segment info. The same pointer is later used with main-image offsets such as 0xC1D2F8, so the published value is the main Core base.
core_offline_open.main_image_target: pacibsp; b 0x3A7D8. Once the slot holds the Core base, CoreRemoteOpen enters the local open body that the public veneer skipped.
core_offline_open.after_call: Reads base+0xC1D2F8 and base+0xC1D300, logs remote.open return=%llx state=%u reason=%s, and returns the local body's result.
core_offline_open.publisher: Walks loaded images. Reads mach_header.filetype at +0xC and keeps MH_EXECUTE (2) whose name comparison with .app/Core returns nonzero, then stores that header at +0x102F0. No direct branch to 0x4B0C exists inside CoreOffline text, and no __mod_init_func section was present.
core_offline_open.null_slot: Before that walk stores a header, the qword remains 0. The sibling at 0x47D0 returns 0 when it is null. CoreRemoteOpen does not make that check.
core_offline_open.shared_gate: Returns 0 when Core+0xC1C258 or +0xC1C259 is set, when 0x2DA7C or fatal/quarantine helper 0x38DF0 reports a block, or when the words at +0xC52E00 and +0xC52E04 are not both at least 1. Otherwise validates three pointers at +0xC52E08, +0xC52E10 and +0xC52E18.
